title: Tenant grace-window memory shepherd for continuous batching
creator: Aisha Varma
description: Implement a tenant-focused grace-window and memory shepherding policy to improve fairness during continuous batching while reducing harmful preemption. The feature should reduce high-latency tail events for small, latency-sensitive tenants without regressing overall throughput or increasing GPU OOM risk. This ticket covers design, runtime implementation, microbenchmarks, and a staged rollout behind a runtime flag.
acceptance_criteria: Per-tenant 95th percentile latency for latency-sensitive customers improves by >=15% under mixed workloads in our lab harness
Overall GPU token throughput reduction <= 3% compared to baseline under steady-state production mixes
No increase in OOM incidents in 48h soak test across dedicated cluster (pass/fail)
Feature gated behind runtime flag and observable via Console dashboard (per-tenant holdback metric)
Unit and integration tests covering eviction decisions, grace expiry, and soft-yield counters
design_decisions: Use a per-tenant 'grace window' allocator: when a tenant is about to be preempted, they receive a short, bounded 'holdback' token budget to finish low-latency requests
Implement a lightweight memory shepherd that tracks estimated key-value residency per tenant using age-buckets (hot, warm, cold) instead of full-size accounting to keep CPU overhead low
Eviction policy: age-bucketed LRU with a tenant-weighted cold-reservation to avoid catastrophic KV churn for latency-sensitive tenants
Admission and preemption will consider both 'soft-yield tokens' (grace budget) and a GPU memory watermark to avoid OOMs
Expose telemetry: per-tenant holdback_used, grace_expirations, eviction_count_by_bucket, and memory_pressure_level
tasks: Spec: document algorithm and API for grace-window in Confluence
Runtime: implement holdback token allocator and shepherd accounting
Runtime: integrate with continuous-batcher preemption hook and soft-yield path
Tests: unit tests for token lifecycle and eviction heuristics
Benchmarks: mixed-workload microbench harness and long-running soak
Console: add dashboard tiles and alerts for grace expirations and memory pressure
Rollout: feature flag + canary on dedicated pool, monitor for regressions
risks: Mis-tuned grace windows could mask fairness problems and let noisy tenants retain hot KV forever
Additional accounting can add CPU overhead and increase latency in the hot path if not kept lightweight
Complex interactions with existing eviction heuristics could cause oscillation between tenants
Incorrect watermarking may still allow OOMs under pathological workloads
